Subject: SIG follow-up: ephemeral session screenshots, runbook, network diagram

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for walking us through the SIG intake earlier. We ran the internal review and have a couple of follow-ups to close our evidence pack for SOC 2 scope: 

- A short set (3–5) of ephemeral session screenshots showing how support engineers access customer environments (redacted IDs).
- The on-call/runbook page that describes session initiation and post-session redaction steps.
- A current network diagram (customer-facing view) that shows where ephemeral sessions terminate.

If possible, please provide Drive links or a zipped bundle and point us to the specific files we should reference in the SIG. Also flag any items that are not shareable and we can work around with an SSC.

Targeting our internal deadline next Wednesday (2027-06-09) — let us know if that works.

Thanks,
Jane

Jane, Jasmine —

Uploaded the initial sanitized bundle to the shared folder. What I included: 
- ephemeral-sessions-screenshots-redacted.zip (screenshots have session IDs and IPs redacted; filenames indicate timestamp)
- sig-runbook-v2.pdf (excerpt: pages 4-7 contain session initiation + post-session redaction checklist)
- network-diagram-canvas.png (customer-facing overlay; internal VLANs removed)

Short notes on redaction: we replaced session IDs with "<REDACTED>" and blurred any ephemeral tokens or ephemeral hostnames. We kept UI flow steps intact so you can confirm process coverage.

If you need a version with stronger anonymization (hashing instead of redaction) I can run that and add a redaction manifest.

Jasmine / team —

Quick read-through from AuditLabs: bundle looks good. A couple of small asks before we mark evidence as "accepted":

- Can you provide a short service-account audit snippet that shows session creation events (timestamp, actor, session_id) for one week? Redact any customer identifiers. A 50–100 line snippet is sufficient.
- In the runbook excerpt, clarify the rollback step after a mistaken redaction (we want the decision point and owner documented).

If you can drop those two items to the same Drive folder we'll be able to close our checklist and provide the SIG attestation language to MedVantage.

Cheers,

Principal Auditor, AuditLabs
